Subject: Private deployment: VPC boundary & control/data-plane handoff for ACME

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re ramping up our private deployment evaluation and want to validate a proposed handoff model: Redwood control plane in vendor-managed cloud (Redwood-hosted control plane) + ACME-managed on-prem data plane inside a dedicated VPC. High level requirements:

- Control plane only needs outgoing connectivity to: KMS endpoints (customer-managed KMS), telemetry/metrics endpoints (Redwood), and DocuSign/other vendor APIs. No inbound connections to control plane from on-prem required.
- Data plane must host inference nodes behind ACME edge routers. All customer data must never traverse public internet unencrypted; egress to telemetry must be optional.
- Mutual TLS for control->data-plane auth, token-based authorizations, and audit logging (retain logs >= 90 days).
- SOC 2 evidence for separation of control/data plane operations and proof that control plane cannot access raw customer data.

We attached our internal requirements doc (acme-deployment-requirements.pdf). Can Redwood provide:
1) A concise diagram showing control-plane endpoints and allowed egress flows for the on-prem data plane.
2) A short runbook for the handoff, including initial network validation checks for MTU, NAT behavior, and expected keep-alive ports.
3) A proposed timeline for a pilot (3–4 nodes) and what we need from our infraops team.

We’re targeting an internal security review next week. Can you loop in anyone from your side who should review network specifics? If useful, CC infraops@acme.com and I can pull our topology.

Thanks,
Laura Roberts
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
ACME Corp

Attachment: acme-deployment-requirements.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Thanks — quick technical notes / clarifying questions that should be in the runbook:

- Control-plane keep-alive: we use a 30s heartbeat over TLS; recommend allowing outbound TCP 443 to the control-plane FQDN from the data-plane nodes. If ACME has strict egress proxying, allowlist by SNI/FQDN is sufficient.
- KV cache sizing: pilot with 3 nodes defaulting to 8GB KV cache each; if workload has long sequences, we’ll need to tune. Marcus to provide a small sizing table.
- NAT behavior: if your edge NAT translates source ports aggressively, consider preserving source port or using a NAT traversal/keepalive strategy — include UDP/TCP port behavior checks in validation.
- Telemetry: option to route telemetry through ACME-managed aggregators (preferred for some customers). We must document the expected telemetry endpoints and the TLS cert pinning options.

I’ll draft the iptables/NACL examples and an MTU verification command snippet. Priyom — can you confirm the cert rotation interval we plan for pilot (we typically recommend 7 days for short-lived pilot certs)?

— Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
